output.brief: Store 14's rise is not yet shown to be real. The Q1–Q3 figures are estimates from partial cycle counts, with an error of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across the chain, about half of the stores that showed two straight rises were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's past full-count results were steady at 1.5–1.8%. The shoplifting log count rose chain-wide after the incident app launched on 1 April, while chain shrink stayed flat, so the store's own increase proves little. Self-checkout and the bus interchange both fit the timing, but nothing here separates them from estimate noise. The ethics-line tip was checked on CCTV and was ordinary cardboard bale runs, so the evidence doesn't support suspending the stocker. The neighbouring stores show no matching rise, which fits a store-specific effect or noise and doesn't settle which. Sales mix is ruled out because it barely changed. What to do next: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and do not drop it, because that is the one measurement that will show whether the loss is real. Hold off on a guard, on pulling or staffing the lanes, and on any personnel action until the count result is compared with the interim figures. If the loss is confirmed, then look at the front-end, the dock and staffing records. I'm fairly sure of this, though not certain.
